nodeData.topic: 🧬 Year 2 · Body in health and disease

children.note: Advanced systems physiology — kidney, acid–base, gut, endocrine, reproduction, neurophysiology and special senses — underpinning care of diabetes, dehydration, pregnancy and neurological illness in Kenya.

Advanced lipid, amino acid, haem and nucleotide metabolism, molecular biology, hormone signalling and nutrition — linking biochemistry to jaundice, malnutrition, drug action and molecular diagnostics.
Principles of laboratory testing and interpretation of electrolytes, acid–base, renal, liver, glucose, bone and protein tests — the everyday results a doctor in Kenya must read correctly.
Foundations of bacteriology, virology and mycology: microbial structure, growth, genetics, sterilisation, antibiotics and resistance, and key bacterial pathogens seen in Kenyan practice.

Basic immunology: cells and organs of immunity, innate defences, complement, antibodies, antigen presentation, T and B cells, cytokines and tolerance – the basis for understanding infection and vaccines.
Principles of pharmacology — pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, adverse reactions, interactions and autonomic drugs — the basis for safe prescribing by every doctor in Kenya.

The general mechanisms of disease: cell injury, inflammation, repair, circulatory disorders, immune injury and neoplasia. The language every Kenyan clinician needs to reason about TB, malaria, cancer and more.
